A1.justification: Both complete 33-page PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–C support reliable comparison; the appendix text and rendered pages are identical.

before.justification: v1 reports original GPT-2 and Llama-2 unlearning experiments, including privacy leakage, utility measurements, and sensitivity analyses in Section 6 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results and reports additional GA learning-rate sweep results in Figure 5.

M1.justification: The minority-aware evaluation procedure, PII-based canary construction, minority selection, and evaluated unlearning algorithms are unchanged. The GA learning-rate sweep concerns evaluation rather than a revised algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Enron-Phone, Enron-Email, and ECHR-Year under Random, Canary, and Minority scenarios. The expanded GA analysis uses existing coverage; the newly cited image-representation work introduces no image experiments.

E2.justification: The comparator membership is unchanged, including within Figure 5: GA already appears as an individual operating point in each v1 panel. v2 expands its tuning and plotted results without introducing a new comparison method.

E3.justification: Section 6.3 and Figure 5 extend the reported trade-off evaluation with a GA learning-rate sweep from 1e-7 to 1e-3. v1 describes sweeps for Langevin and SCRUB and shows individual GA points. The shared benchmark settings, splits, metrics, and computation budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure 5 extends the privacy–utility sensitivity analysis by examining GA across learning rates and displaying its Pareto frontiers. The existing unlearning-iteration, forget-set-size, complexity-budget, and appendix analyses are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions specify random seed 42 in Appendix B.2. The additional GA results introduce no repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or other uncertainty-reporting changes.

E6.justification: Figure 5 adds GA operating points and Pareto frontiers for GPT-2 on Enron-Phone and Enron-Email under Min-K%. These are additional results across configurations, not same-setting performance improvements. Numerical tables and the other figures retain their results.

T1.justification: The unlearning definitions, privacy-leakage equation, algorithm objectives, and computation-budget definitions are unchanged. No theorem, proof, or mathematical derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the claims about underestimated minority privacy risks, minority-aware evaluation, GA instability, and favorable Langevin trade-offs. Naming SCRUB and GA explicitly in the revised introduction clarifies comparisons already claimed in v1.

C2.justification: Both versions interpret minority risk through memorization and describe GA as less reliable across settings than stable alternatives. The revised trade-off paragraph preserves the existing interpretation of GA's weaker Enron-Email performance and adds no substantive limitation.

D1.justification: Section 6.3 newly specifies the GA learning-rate search range, 1e-7 to 1e-3. Other implementation details, hardware disclosures, and appendix hyperparameters are unchanged; Appendix C.6 still details Langevin and SCRUB tuning.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Zhao et al. (2024), What Makes Unlearning Hard and What to Do About It, and briefly connects its image-representation memorization study with this paper's findings for text minorities. The remaining research positioning is retained.

P1.justification: Local edits expand related work, clarify the introduction's trade-off comparison, and rewrite the opening privacy–utility discussion in Section 6.3. The section organization and most prose, including the appendices, remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 5 adds GA frontier lines and legend entries and extends the Enron-Phone horizontal axis. Layout reflow moves Table 4 from page 8 to 9 and Figure 4 from page 9 to 10. Other figure content and appendix layouts are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 improves the trade-off comparison by evaluating GA across learning rates rather than relying on isolated operating points, and it states the search range. This better supports assessment of GA alongside tuned Langevin and SCRUB. The added related-work discussion improves positioning, while the unchanged central study and appendices keep the overall gain limited.
